title: Witness d = 𝑅ᵣ∞ ρ for the generalized quantum Stein's lemma (Theorem 4)
intent: Close the file's headline theorem — Theorem 4, the generalized quantum Stein's lemma stated as the existence of one number to which both the hypothesis-testing rate and the regularized relative entropy of resource converge — by naming the witness d = 𝑅ᵣ∞ ρ and discharging the two convergences of the conjunction with the two project lemmas that already prove them.

parent.name: limit_hypotesting_eq_limit_rel_entropy
parent.statement:
theorem limit_hypotesting_eq_limit_rel_entropy (ρ : MState (H i)) (ε : Prob) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1) :
    ∃ d : ℝ≥0,
      Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ —log β_ ε(ρ ⊗ᵣ^[n]‖IsFree) / n) (𝓝 d)
      ∧
      Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (⨅ σ ∈ IsFree, 𝐃(ρ ⊗ᵣ^[n]‖σ)) / n) (𝓝 d)

children.name: GeneralizedQSteinsLemma
children.statement:
theorem GeneralizedQSteinsLemma {i : ι} (ρ : MState (H i)) {ε : Prob} (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1) :
    Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ —log β_ ε(ρ ⊗ᵣ^[n]‖IsFree) / n) (𝓝 (𝑅ᵣ∞ ρ))

children.name: RelativeEntResource.tendsto_ennreal
children.statement:
theorem RelativeEntResource.tendsto_ennreal (ρ : MState (H i)) :
    Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (⨅ σ ∈ IsFree, 𝐃(ρ ⊗ᵣ^[n]‖σ)) / ↑n) (𝓝 (𝑅ᵣ∞ ρ))
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the regularized relative entropy of resource (⨅ σ ∈ IsFree, 𝐃(ρ ⊗ᵣ^[n] ‖ σ)) / n tends to 𝑅ᵣ∞ ρ

applicability.goal_shape: ∃ d : ℝ≥0, (seq₁ n ⟶ d) ∧ (seq₂ n ⟶ d): two sequences are each already known by a named project lemma to converge to the same concrete term (here the regularized relative entropy of resource 𝑅ᵣ∞ ρ).
applicability.use_when: each conjunct is already proved as a named lemma with exactly the target's statement, so the only remaining work is to exhibit the common witness and conjoin the two facts.
applicability.avoid_when: the two limits are not yet known to coincide, or a conjunct must be proved from scratch (then the work lives in the child lemma and the witness is not the point); when the common limit is not a concrete term but only obtained via completeness, so there is no term available to `use`.

claims.claim: The witness move closes the parent in 5 lines of proof (2119-2123: one `use` naming d, one `constructor` splitting the conjunction, one `exact` per conjunct) from two named project lemmas whose proofs are 129 lines (GeneralizedQSteinsLemma, 1980-2108) and 8 lines (RelativeEntResource.tendsto_ennreal, FreeState.lean 481-488); the checked lemma chain below the parent is 4 deep (limit_hypotesting_eq_limit_rel_entropy → GeneralizedQSteinsLemma → Lemma7_gap → Lemma7 → EquationS62).
claims.evidence: line counts of the parent by-block (2119-2123) and the two child sites (1980-2108 and FreeState.lean 481-488), counted from the copied files; the chain is cited at 2122, 2032, 1971, 1948 of SteinsLemma.lean

claims.claim: The authors state that they prove the generalized quantum Stein's lemma as the existence of one number to which both sides converge, rather than as an equality of limits: "What they state as an equality of limits, which don't exist per se in Mathlib, we state as the existence of a number (which happens to be `RegularizedRelativeEntResource`) to which both sides converge."

metrics.how_counted: child_lines = the two child site spans (1980-1981 for GeneralizedQSteinsLemma's statement, 481-488 for tendsto_ennreal's declaration+proof); child_proof_lines = the full declaration+proof spans (1980-2108 and 481-488), counted from the copied files

consequences: The `use` commits to one witness and `constructor` creates the two conjuncts as obligations, each discharged by a lemma that must prove convergence to exactly that d; a lemma that converges to a different spelling of the same limit needs a `convert`/`congr`. There is no exhaustiveness obligation (that belongs to case-split) and no induction. The honesty of the move rests entirely on the two child lemmas being closed and about the same limit; if the second conjunct (the ⨅ σ ∈ IsFree, 𝐃(ρ ⊗ᵣ^[n] ‖ σ) / n side) were unproved, the witness move would reduce the theorem to a still-hard child rather than close it.
